methodNote: Two independently-created documents with byte-identical Section 6.01 headed 'Payment Conditions', subsection 6.01(a), a defined term 'Payment Conditions', and a $100,000,000 threshold - once across two companies (Tenant A/B), once across two facilities in one company. Real Postgres, no mocks. Test ids prefixed audit-a-, verified cleaned up after run.

tests.attackVector: definitions (DefinedTermNode) across two instruments in ONE company
tests.summary: Only ONE DefinedTermNode row survives for two facilities both defining 'Payment Conditions'; the row is internally contradictory - documentId frozen at Facility Alpha (create-time), sourceNodeId (the real citation anchor) silently points into Facility Beta.
tests.counterexample: computeStableKey('defined-term', companyId, normalizedTerm) at lib/contract-model/compiler/persistence.ts:156,171 omits documentId/instrument scoping entirely, unlike DocumentNode's stableKey (includes charStart, 3F.1.2) and ContractRule's (includes sourceDocumentId).
tests.corroboration: Independently re-discovered by WS7's fault-injection workstream (see FAULT_INJECTION_RESULTS 'cross-document definition collision at PERSISTENCE layer'), which classified it P1 rather than P0. This audit reconciles the disagreement in favor of P0: the defect produces silent, internally-contradictory persisted state that misattributes a real definition to the wrong instrument with zero error signal, meeting this audit's own P0 bar ('silent corruption... without warning').

tests.summary: validateTenantIsolation (lib/contract-model/validators.ts:128-162) only checks targetRuleId, DocumentRelationshipEdge, and AmendmentEffect for cross-tenant leakage - never ContractReferenceEdge.targetTermId or targetDocumentNodeId. An injected cross-tenant edge via those fields passes clean.

getRulesByCovenantFamily returns both facilities' rules merged into one undifferentiated array; ContractRule carries no instrumentId column. Not a leak (both legitimately belong to the company) but no way to ask for just one instrument's rules.

6 service.ts functions (getAmendmentsForDocument, getSupplementsForDocument, getRelatedDocuments, getModificationCandidates, findDocumentsReferencing, getDocumentsForInstrument) take a bare id with no companyId check. Zero current production callers (grep-confirmed) - latent IDOR-shaped gap, not exploitable today.
Zero prisma.* calls under discovery/** - pure in-memory, per-call companyId parameter, nothing to leak through.

compile.ts's module-level defaultCache (used by every real current caller that omits options.cache) is keyed by cache.ts's computeCacheKey, which never includes companyId/instrumentKey/sourceDocumentId. Company B's compile request was served Company A's cached result with the model never invoked for Company B. Currently latent (no app/ route wired), but is the default for the entire semantic-compiler surface.
tests.corroboration: Independently confirmed by WS7 (SUSPICIOUS_PATTERN_INVENTORY) via a separate code-inspection method reaching the same conclusion.

tests.summary: Pure functions over a caller-supplied OperativeContractState - architecturally sound (no shared state), but this workstream did not construct a full adversarial cross-instrument amendment chain to positively prove it end-to-end.

lib/covenant-engine.ts (the LIVE legacy engine powering the dashboard today) has zero instrumentId/instrumentKey/Facility concept in its Prisma queries - every query is companyId-scoped only. Whether this causes actual computational conflation of two instruments' covenant capacity, or is safe because each Permission is already independently evaluated, requires solver-internals tracing beyond this workstream's time budget. Honestly reported as inconclusive rather than rounded up.
